RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.ArchivesSourc:
# SECURE ARCHIVES

Omega authorization confirmed. The following documents were isolated from the central network after the incident.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.Communication:
# INTERNAL COMMUNICATIONS

## 17 OCT 1979 — VOSS > TANNHÄUSER

The Laboratory B sensor network is still returning impossible data. Do not restart anything before I arrive.

## 18 OCT 1979 — WARD > VOSS

Three team members describe the same dream. They all repeat coordinates 04-19-22.

## UNSENT MESSAGE — TANNHÄUSER

I placed temporary access on the archives: `ORPHEE-79`. If the system erases my records, someone must be able to recover them.

RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.DiagnosticsSo:
# CORE DIAGNOSTICS

Running `ORPHEUS-DIAG --deep`…

- Core memory: 97%
- Internal network: unstable
- External sensors: nominal
- Laboratory B: inconsistent response

::effect glitch
WARNING // Video loop B-04 contains 11 seconds that correspond to no station clock.
::end

Signal origin: **INTERNAL**.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.IncidentSourc:
# INCIDENT 1979

Classification: OMEGA-BLACK. On October 18, a Laboratory B door opened for 11 seconds despite its mechanical lock. No access was recorded.

The team first concluded that an external intruder was responsible. Radio logs prove the command signal was already originating inside the laboratory.

Commander Voss ordered the report erased, then disappeared six hours later.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.LabLogSource:
# RECOVERED LOG — LABORATORY B

`[18-10-1979 03:14:02]` The specimen reacts to the navigation signal.

`[03:14:07]` It does not reproduce sounds. It reproduces the intentions behind sounds.

`[03:14:11]` Ward requests evacuation. Voss refuses: the exterior door is no longer a safe exit.

`[03:14:13]` A second voice uses Voss’s identifier from inside the empty chamber.

**END OF FILE — 38% OF DATA UNRECOVERABLE**
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.LaboratoryInd:
# PUBLIC LABORATORY INDEX

- Laboratory A: mineral analysis and isotope dating
- Laboratory B: xenobiology and environmental containment
- Laboratory C: gravitational cartography
- Hydroponic greenhouse: food crops and control samples

Laboratory B visits are suspended for maintenance. Direct inquiries to Medical Services on the Science Deck.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.MainSource:
# SECURITY CONSOLE — ORPHEUS STATION

Maintenance session established. Last complete synchronization: **18 OCT 1979**.

Warning: several sectors contain restored or intentionally hidden data.

Select a subsystem.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.PersonnelSour:
# PERSONNEL FILES

Duty team registry for the science sector at the time of the incident.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.PublicAccessS:
# STATION PUBLIC NETWORK

Welcome aboard Orpheus Station. This section requires no clearance and may be explored freely.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.QuarantineSou:
# QUARANTINE PROTOCOL Q-7

- Physically seal Laboratory B.
- Cut every radio and optical relay.
- Do not answer a voice coming from a room declared empty.
- Require two visual confirmations before opening a door.
- If two crew members share the same biometric identifier, isolate both subjects.

Ward’s handwritten note: *The protocol assumes we still know which one is human.*
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.ScienceDeckSo:
# SCIENCE DECK

Sector 04 — research, infirmary, and quarantine. Public access is limited to directories and service schedules.

::menu children
::end
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.StationOvervi:
# ORPHEUS STATION

Orpheus is an autonomous scientific platform operating at the edge of the Hecate system. Its official mission is to map gravitational anomalies and study organisms recovered by long-range probes.

Nominal capacity: 42 crew. Commissioned: March 12, 1974. Operational authority: Commander Lena Voss.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.StatusSource:
# SYSTEM STATUS

- Main reactor: STANDBY
- Life support: 61% — 19 hours remaining
- Long-range communications: OFFLINE
- Artificial gravity: NOMINAL
- Detected crew: 1
- Active personal transponders: 2

**Unresolved anomaly: the number of transponders exceeds the number of life signs.**
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.TannhauserSou:
# MARC TANNHÄUSER — SYSTEMS ENGINEER

Clearance: BETA-4. Responsible for sensors, robotic maintenance, and local backups.

Last activity: created temporary Omega access minutes before the general failure. His personal terminal contains eleven deletion attempts rejected by the core.

Automated annotation: *User likely aware of the falsified Laboratory B logs.*

RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.VossSource:
# LENA VOSS — COMMANDER

Clearance: OMEGA. Seventeen years of service without a disciplinary incident.

Last confirmed access: Laboratory B, October 18, 1979 at 03:12. At 03:26, her transponder was detected simultaneously in the laboratory and on the bridge.

Voss classified the incident and ordered that no one answer calls originating from her own identifier.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Example.WardSource:
# DR ELISE WARD — CHIEF MEDICAL OFFICER

Clearance: BETA-3. Specialist in sleep neurology and xenobiological exposure.

Ward reported identical memories in three technicians who had never worked together. Her final medical report ends in the middle of a sentence.

Transcribed audio note: *This is not an infection. It is a repetition.*
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Enabled: Disable to hide this terminal everywhere without deleting anything.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Label: Name shown in the launcher and in the terminal header.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.TerminalId: Generated from the name. Change it only if a macro or a link already uses another value.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.StartPage: Page opened by Home and by the launcher.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Theme: Base preset for every page of this terminal.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Published: Published terminals appear in the players' launcher. Journal permissions still apply.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Sort: Lower values are listed first in the launcher.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Icon: Font Awesome classes, for example fa-solid fa-satellite-dish.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.BootSequence: Plays a short start-up animation the first time the terminal opens.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.RememberPage: Reopens each user on the last page they visited.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.CloseAtRoot: Escape closes the window instead of doing nothing on the home page.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Preset: Loading a preset overwrites every control below.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.PageId: Lowercase identifier used by ::menu links, for example incident-1979.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.PageType: Changes how the page is presented; it does not restrict the markup.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.MenuLabel: Text used by parent menus. Falls back to the page name.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Parent: The page whose ::menu children directive should list this page.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.PageSort: Lower values are listed first inside the parent menu.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.ShowInMenu: Uncheck to keep the page reachable by link only.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Visibility: A hidden page disappears from automatic menus and cannot be opened by players.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Access: A locked page stays listed but asks for its unlock before opening.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.LockType: GM only reserves the page for gamemasters; Password prompts every other user.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Password: Stored in clear text and readable by anyone allowed to view the page. Treat it as a prop, not as a security control.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.FailureMessage: Shown in place of the page when the code is refused.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.Source: Terminal markup. Drop a Journal or a page to insert a link.
RETRO_CRT_TERMINAL.Hints.ThemeOverride: Replaces the terminal theme for this page only.
